reader.decision: Keep `legacy_sku` for now. Do not drop the column and run no migration. Re-key with Oakline Supply is not started until they agree.
reader.decision_reason: The message says `v_partner_feed` and the nightly export read `legacy_sku`, and it is the only store of the Brightstock codes that Oakline Supply uses. A drop would either break the feed or send codes the partner cannot match, while keeping the column costs one nullable text column.

reconstruction.problem: I wanted to drop `legacy_sku` from `products` because my grep of `src/` found no use. The message says the column is still used. `v_partner_feed` reads it as `COALESCE(p.legacy_sku, p.sku) AS partner_ref`. The nightly `partner_feed_export` job sends that to Oakline Supply over SFTP. Oakline Supply keys its catalog on the Brightstock codes, and only `legacy_sku` stores them. The importer `brightstock_import.py` also names the column, but it ran once, on 12 March 2024.
reconstruction.what_breaks: A plain DROP is rejected because the view depends on the column. With CASCADE the view is dropped and the nightly export fails, so no feed reaches Oakline Supply. If the view is rewritten to `p.sku AS partner_ref`, the job runs but the 6,140 migrated products carry new codes. Oakline Supply cannot match them, so their prices and items go stale or are rejected.
reconstruction.fix: Keep the column and run no migration. `db/schema.sql`, `db/views.sql` and the importer stay unchanged. The alternative is to have Oakline Supply re-key its catalog to `sku` first. After that, change the view to `p.sku AS partner_ref`, drop the column and delete the importer.
reconstruction.cost: Keeping the column costs one nullable text column and nothing breaks. The re-key alternative costs a coordinated change with an external partner. No timeline or effort estimate is stated.

reader.closing_answer: I keep `legacy_sku` for now. I do not start the re-key plan until Oakline Supply agrees to move its catalog to `sku`.
